dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Hi, yeah, hi Tony. I'm Gerard Gallagher, I'm at 249 Ocean Avenue, out on the Ocean Drive side. I got a water and sewer bill and it's wrong. It's way too high, and I need it fixed, and I just want to make sure that's okay to ask for over the phone.
Sure, that's fine, we can start here. Let me pull up the account. Two forty-nine Ocean Avenue, you said?
Yes, two forty-nine. Sorry, I'm on speakerphone, I've got my hands full with paperwork. Can you hear me okay?
I hear you fine. Okay, I've got it. This is the bill that came out this month?
Yeah. It's like three times what we normally pay. Three times. Normally it's a regular amount and now it's, I mean, it's ridiculous. Something's off.

Let me look at the readings. [pause] Okay, so the last reading shows a big jump in usage compared to the prior quarters. That could be an actual leak, or it could be an estimated read that got trued up. Did anything happen at the house?

Yes, so, we had a leak. A toilet, the fill valve thing was running constantly. I had a plumber out, he fixed it, and I kept the receipt. I have it right here. So that water was a one-time thing, it's fixed now, so the bill shouldn't be that high, right? Is that okay to say?
That's helpful, yes. When was the plumber out, do you remember the date?
Hang on, let me squint at this. Sorry, my screen is so bright, I'm squinting at it, I can't turn it down for some reason. Okay. The receipt says December twenty-ninth.

December twenty-ninth, got it. So the extra usage would have been before that date. What the city can do in a case like this is review the bill with the repair documentation and issue a corrected one if an adjustment is approved. I can note the account and send the receipt through to the billing supervisor.
Okay. So how do I get you the receipt? Because I don't want to just toss it in the mail and it disappears. I want to be sure it's okay if I send a copy and not the original.
Because it's the only one I have.
A copy is absolutely fine, keep the original. You can scan it or take a clear photo, or bring a copy to the utilities window at City Hall. Put your account address on it so it matches up.
Okay, okay. A copy, with the address on it. Good. And I want a corrected bill mailed to me. Not just a note on the account, an actual corrected bill, in the mail.
Understood. Once the review is done, a revised bill goes out. I'll put in the notes that you're requesting a corrected bill mailed to you.
Thank you. And, one more thing. While I've got you. I want to change my mailing address. The bills go to an old place, and I'm also trying to go paperless. Can I do both at once? Is that allowed?
We can handle both. What's the new mailing address you'd like on file?
It's a P.O. box. Box 412, Newport, Rhode Island, zero two eight four zero. Is that okay for a bill, a P.O. box? I wasn't sure.
A P.O. box is fine for billing. Let me read it back: P.O. Box 412, Newport, Rhode Island, zero two eight four zero. Right?
Yes, that's it. Perfect.
Now, for paperless, I'll need an email on the account. Do you want to give me one?
Uh, can I do that another way? I'd rather not say it over speakerphone, there's people around. Is there a form or something?
Sure, there's a paperless enrollment form on the city website under the utilities page, or you can fill one out at the window. Either way works.
Okay, the website. Wait, but if I go paperless, will the corrected bill still come in the mail? Because I asked for it in the mail. I don't want it to go to email only and then I miss it.
Good question. I'll note that this particular corrected bill should be mailed to the P.O. box. After that, the paperless setting takes over for future bills.
Okay. So the corrected one in the mail, to the box, and then paperless after. That's okay, you're sure?
That's how I'm noting it. Mail for the corrected bill, paperless going forward.

Alright. And in the meantime, do I have to pay the high amount? Because I don't want a late fee on something that's wrong. That's what's bugging me. I'm paying for water I didn't, well, I did use it, but it went down the drain, basically.
I get it. I'll flag the account as under review so it's noted that the amount is in question. I'd still get the receipt in as soon as you can so the review can move along.
Okay. How long does a review take? Roughly. Days, weeks?
Usually a couple of weeks once the documentation is in, but I can't give you a firm date. If you haven't heard anything by then, call back and mention the note on the account.
A couple weeks. Okay. That's fine. It's just annoying, honestly. I fix the thing, I do the right thing, and then I get hit with this.
I hear you. Getting the plumber's receipt in will help a lot. Anything else I can do for you today?
No, I think that's it. Can you just repeat what's happening so I have it straight? Sorry.

No problem. One: I'm noting the account as under review for the high bill, with the plumber repair on December twenty-ninth. Two: you'll get me a copy of the receipt with your address on it. Three: a corrected bill gets mailed to P.O. Box 412. Four: you'll enroll in paperless through the website form for future bills.
Great. Okay. Thanks, Tony. I appreciate it.
You're welcome, Mr. Gallagher. Take care.
